tagline: The Wiley Fox guide to London for families and solo travellers
cover_blurb: What 13 travel creators actually say about London, checked against the latest police data - where to stay, where to take care, how to get around and what it costs.

safety.wf_summary: London is a well-policed city and most visits pass without trouble. The main risk for visitors is theft: pickpocketing and phone snatching in the busiest central areas. Violence against tourists is rare and concentrated late at night around nightlife and some outer town centres.
safety.creator_summary: Every creator we reviewed describes London as comfortable for visitors, including families. The repeated warnings are practical ones: watch your phone near the kerb, keep bags zipped in crowds, never leave a phone on a pub table, and look right before you cross.
safety.data_note: Recorded crimes are the monthly average for May to July 2026 within roughly one mile of each area centre (data.police.uk). Busy tourist areas record more crime partly because far more people pass through them; the circles for Soho, Covent Garden, Leicester Square and Oxford Street overlap.

app_ctas.text: Check any hotel street on the Wiley Fox map before you book - tap it for the latest month of recorded crime nearby.
Clip a Wiley Fox QR wristband on each child. If you get separated in a crowd, anyone who scans it can contact you straight away - no app needed on their side.
Heading back late? Use Safest Route on thewileyfox.com to pick a better-lit, lower-crime walk to your hotel, and keep SOS one tap away.
Seen something other travellers should know? Drop a community report on the map - it helps rate the area for the next family.

overview: London is huge - more a region than a city - so the single best decision you make is where you stay. Creators agree on one rule above all others: book within a ten-minute walk of a Tube station, and group each day by neighbourhood rather than criss-crossing town.

For families it is one of the easiest capitals in the world. The big museums are free, the parks are enormous, and the Tube, buses and river boats reach almost everything. Children under 11 travel free on the Tube and buses with a paying adult.

For solo travellers it is lively every night of the week. The risks are ordinary big-city ones, and they cluster in predictable places. This guide shows you where, using the same police data that powers the Wiley Fox map.

facts.Currency: Pound sterling (GBP) - almost everywhere is contactless
facts.Entry: Many visitors now need a UK ETA - £20 since April 2026
facts.Tipping: 12.5% service is usually already on the bill

stay.why: Walk to the Natural History Museum, Science Museum and V&A - all free. Leafy, residential and well connected on three Tube lines.
Next to Kensington Gardens and the Diana Memorial Playground. Calmer than the West End, still zone 1.
Big Ben, the London Eye and the river walk to Tower Bridge on foot. Busy by day, so recorded theft is high - keep bags zipped on Westminster Bridge.
Village feel on Marylebone High Street, minutes from Oxford Street without its crowds. The data circle includes Oxford Street, which inflates the count.
Royal Observatory, a free view over the whole city and a riverboat commute into town.
The lowest recorded crime of every area we checked. Richmond has the river and Petersham Meadows; both are 20-45 minutes from central London by train.
London's best-connected hub, with six Tube lines and Eurostar. Busy around the station at night; the canal-side Granary Square area is calmer.
Borough Market, riverside pubs and quick links everywhere. Bermondsey next door has a quieter, village feel.
Street art, food and nightlife. Great for a younger solo trip - plan your late-night route home.

caution.area: Leicester Square, Soho, Covent Garden & Oxford Street
caution.when: All day, busiest evenings and weekends
caution.note: The highest recorded crime in our sample, and nearly half of it is theft. Phone snatching by riders on e-bikes is the number-one warning from creators. Pedicab (rickshaw) drivers are unregulated - agree the price before you get in, or better, don't.

caution.area: Westminster Bridge & the South Bank by the London Eye
caution.note: Prime pickpocket territory and the spot for the shell-and-cup street game. You will never win it - the 'winners' are part of the act.

caution.when: Late evening, around the station and main road
caution.note: Brick Lane and the markets are worth a daytime visit. Recorded crime is lower than the West End, but violence and anti-social behaviour make up a larger share. Some creators suggest it as a budget base; with children or a late arrival, we'd stay further west.
Violence is the top recorded category here. Cheap 'central London' hotel deals are often in Croydon - a long commute and not where we'd base a family trip.
Not a visitor area. A third of recorded crime is violence or robbery, the highest share in our sample. There's no reason to base a trip here.
Very crowded at weekends, with theft and anti-social behaviour on the high street. For independent shops without the crush, locals point to Camden Passage by Angel instead.

scams.title: Phone snatching
scams.text: Riders on e-bikes grab phones from people walking near the kerb. Step into a shop doorway to check maps, and keep your phone on the building side.

scams.title: Pub table theft
scams.text: Phones and wallets left on tables vanish in seconds. Keep bags in front of you or under the table, never on the back of your chair.

scams.title: Pedicab overcharging
scams.text: Rickshaws in the West End have charged tourists hundreds of pounds for short rides. There is no regulated fare.

scams.title: Street games & 'free' gifts
scams.text: The shell game, a 'found' ring or a free bracelet always ends with someone wanting money.

scams.title: Fake petitions & charity collectors
scams.text: Clipboard petitions around the sights are often a set-up for a donation or a distraction. A polite 'no thanks' and keep walking.

scams.title: Currency conversion at ATMs and card machines
scams.text: Always choose to pay in pounds. Letting the machine convert to your home currency can cost far more.

scams.title: Unofficial theatre tickets
scams.text: Buy from the theatre box office, TodayTix or the official TKTS booth in Leicester Square - not from people on the street.

transport.title: From the airport
transport.text: Heathrow is on the Piccadilly and Elizabeth lines - tap your card and go. Creators rate the Heathrow Express as quick but poor value unless you are staying at Paddington. Check late-night options before booking a cheap arrival into Stansted or Luton; the last trains can leave you with an expensive taxi.

transport.title: Pay with contactless
transport.text: Tap the same card or phone in and out. Daily caps are applied automatically: £8.90 a day for zones 1-2 on Tube and rail, frozen until March 2027. Paper tickets and paper day Travelcards cost more.

transport.title: Buses
transport.text: £1.75 a ride with unlimited changes within an hour (the Hopper fare). Routes 11 and 24 pass many of the big sights and make a cheap sightseeing tour from the top deck.

transport.title: Children
transport.text: Under-11s travel free on the Tube and buses with a paying adult. Avoid the Tube at 7:30-9am and 5-7pm with small children and pushchairs.

transport.title: Taxis
transport.text: Black cabs are licensed and heavily regulated - if the orange light is on, it's free. Free Now books licensed cabs by app and shows the fare estimate. Ignore unlicensed minicabs that approach you in the street.

transport.title: By river
transport.text: The Uber Boat (Thames Clippers) is part of the public network - tap in and ride to Greenwich or the Tower. A relaxing option when little legs are tired.

transport.title: Walk more
transport.text: Many central Tube stops are only 5-15 minutes apart on foot. Victoria to Buckingham Palace, for example, is faster walking. Stand on the right on escalators.

transport.title: Late at night
transport.text: If you're on your own late, a licensed cab is worth the money over a long walk. Plan the route home before you head out - Wiley Fox's Safest Route helps.

costs.item: Espresso at Algerian Coffee Stores, Soho

top.name: The free museums
top.why: The Natural History Museum, Science Museum, V&A and British Museum are free. Book a free time slot online to skip the queue.

top.name: Tower of London
top.why: Crown Jewels and Beefeater stories. The evening Ceremony of the Keys is a few pounds but sells out a month ahead.

top.name: Free sky-high views
top.why: Sky Garden and Horizon 22 are free but need booking in advance. Sky Garden is higher than the London Eye.

top.name: Changing the Guard
top.why: Not every day - check the official schedule the week before. Arrive early and watch your bag in the crowd.

top.name: Thames path: London Eye to Tower Bridge
top.why: The classic riverside walk past Tate Modern, Shakespeare's Globe and Borough Market.

top.name: Greenwich & the Royal Observatory
top.why: One of the best free city views, stand on the Prime Meridian, and arrive by river boat.

top.name: Diana Memorial Playground
top.why: A pirate-ship playground next to Kensington Palace - a favourite for under-12s.

top.name: Regent's Canal walk
top.why: A traffic-free towpath through Camden. The Paddington to King's Cross stretch suits families.

top.name: A West End show
top.why: Enter ticket lotteries and check TodayTix for same-day deals. Skip the street touts.

top.name: Harry Potter Studio Tour
top.why: About an hour north of London - book weeks ahead, it sells out.

eat.name: Regency Café
eat.why: A time-warp caff that has starred in films. A full breakfast for about the price of a sourdough loaf elsewhere - have your order ready.

eat.name: Bun House
eat.why: Filled steamed buns - pork, veggie and a custard one that children love.

eat.name: Four Seasons (Wardour Street)
eat.why: The place for roast duck and roast pork over rice.

eat.name: Arcade Food Hall
eat.why: Eight kitchens under one roof - easy when everyone wants something different. Upstairs, Plaza Khao Gaeng (Michelin-listed southern Thai) does one of London's best beef massaman curries.

eat.name: Seashell of Lisson Grove
eat.why: A long-running chippy on TOPJAW's fish and chips list - near Regent's Park and Baker Street.

eat.name: Dishoom
eat.area: Several sites incl. Covent Garden & King's Cross
eat.why: The London Indian restaurant creators send everyone to. Expect a queue at peak times.

eat.name: Homeslice
eat.why: Giant shareable pizzas a few steps from Covent Garden - a better bet than Leicester Square chains.

eat.name: Beigel Bake
eat.why: The salt beef bagel is a London rite of passage. A good daytime stop on a Brick Lane visit.

eat.name: Crisp Pizza
eat.why: TOPJAW's pick for London's best pizza. Book a couple of weeks ahead; they suggest the Picante and the hot-honey Vecna.

eat.name: Pophams
eat.why: Pastries baked on site all day. The order: a cardamom bun and a black americano.

eat.name: Donia
eat.why: Upstairs in Kingly Court. Try the ube choux for dessert.

eat.name: The Harwood Arms
eat.why: Chefs' choice for a Sunday roast. Book well ahead.

grown_ups: For a grown-ups' night out, TOPJAW's chef interviews point to The Devonshire in Soho for a pint of Guinness and the Connaught Bar in Mayfair for a martini.

hotels.name: The Rubens at the Palace
hotels.why: Opposite the Royal Mews, walking distance to Buckingham Palace and St James's Park.

hotels.name: Park Plaza County Hall
hotels.why: Family rooms beside the London Eye and the river path.

hotels.name: The Ampersand Hotel
hotels.why: A short walk to three free museums in the calmest of the central areas we checked.

hotels.name: St James' Court, A Taj Hotel
hotels.why: Quiet courtyard hotel near Buckingham Palace - used as a base by Curly Tales.

hotels.name: The Hoxton, Holborn
hotels.why: A buzzy lobby with good wifi, walkable to Covent Garden and the British Museum. Camden David rates the Hoxton brand.

hotels.name: citizenM Tower of London
hotels.why: Compact rooms beside the Tower and the river, on the District and Circle lines.

1day: Big Ben and Westminster Abbey, then walk to Buckingham Palace for Changing the Guard (check it's on).
Regency Café for a proper fry-up, or pick up a meal deal for a picnic in St James's Park.
Cross the river and walk the Thames path past Tate Modern to Borough Market.
Walk over Tower Bridge and on to the Tower of London at golden hour.
Chinatown: Four Seasons for roast duck and Bun House for dessert. Keep phones away on the busy streets.
3day: Westminster, Buckingham Palace, St James's Park, then the Thames path to Borough Market.
Tower of London and Tower Bridge.
Chinatown and a West End show.
Natural History Museum and V&A (free, book a slot).
Kensington Gardens and the Diana Memorial Playground.
Dinner at Dishoom or Homeslice in Covent Garden.
Uber Boat to Greenwich and the Royal Observatory.
Sky Garden or Horizon 22 (pre-booked) and a Leadenhall Market wander.
Shoreditch for food; plan a cab or Safest Route home.

tips.title: Look right
tips.text: Traffic drives on the left. Wolters World has seen tourists hit stepping out the wrong way - follow the 'look right' markings.

tips.title: Book the free stuff
tips.text: Sky Garden, Horizon 22 and museum time slots are free but go fast. Book as soon as your dates are set.

tips.title: Don't overload days
tips.text: One or two paid sights a day, grouped by area. London rewards wandering.

tips.title: Skip the 'awful four' combo
tips.text: Love and London's name for pricey ticket bundles (Dungeon, Shrek, Aquarium, Madame Tussauds). Fine for small kids; poor value otherwise.

tips.title: Keep kids out of phone boxes
tips.text: The famous red boxes are often used as toilets. Photo outside, not in.

tips.title: Tag the kids
tips.text: A Wiley Fox QR wristband on each child means anyone who finds them can reach you in seconds.
